key_insight: HVOF-sprayed FeCoCrNiAl high-entropy alloy coating reduced TC4 sliding wear from 25–300 °C, with peak reductions of 49.3% in maximum wear depth and 42.4% in wear volume at 200 °C.
engineering_relevance: The coating offers a route to improve the elevated-temperature sliding-wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V components.
method: Deposit FeCoCrNiAl coating on TC4 using HVOF thermal spraying.
Evaluate reciprocating sliding friction, wear morphology, and damage from 25–300 °C.
Simulate progressive wear using an Archard-based finite element model with ALE adaptive meshing.
evidence_signal: Coated specimens showed lower friction and less severe surface damage at all tested temperatures, while simulated wear profiles deviated from experiments by less than 5%.
watch_item: Localized inter-splat delamination remained a coating damage mechanism; performance beyond the tested temperature range and sliding conditions is unverified.
paper_title: Temperature-dependent tribological performance of HVOF-thermal sprayed FeCoCrNiAl HEA coating deposited on TC4 alloy
